data.description:
Chain link 3, "produces a contract for a client" — server side. A template registry with declared variable slots, substitution into a stored contract record, and a plain HTML render of the generated contract. ONE template in v1 — an independent-contractor-agreement shape — because one closes the chain and a second does not (Rule 1).

IMPLEMENTS: docs/engineering/00-d1-v1-milestone-plan.md section 3 rows C-17 (template set), C-18 (CC BY 4.0 attribution mechanism, IN by mandate) and C-19 (contract generation).

DECISION CONTEXT, INCLUDING A HARD GATE. The intended template source is Common Paper's standard agreements, whose licence the D1 spike verified verbatim from the publisher's own page as CC BY 4.0 — commercial use and adaptation permitted, with attribution (docs/strategy/spikes/spike-D1-freelancer-invoicing.md section 2). The residual the CEO's C5 flagged is still open: ADAPTED TEMPLATE TEXT MUST NOT BE SHOWN TO A REAL USER before a lawyer-agent review clears it. That review is company-level, non-Lattice work (CLAUDE.md scope) — it is a gate on this capability, not a task here, and it is owned by CEO + CTO.

So this task ships CLEARLY-MARKED PLACEHOLDER BODY TEXT: structurally complete, legally inert, visibly labelled as placeholder — while building the attribution mechanism now so the obligation cannot be forgotten when real text lands. The attribution line is exercised by the placeholder and covered by a test. Do not paste adapted Common Paper prose into this task.

VERIFICATION: unit tests — every declared variable is substituted; an unfilled required variable is an error, not a silent blank; the rendered document contains both the attribution line and the placeholder marking; generation is deterministic for identical inputs. No accounts, no network, no Stripe.

NOT IN THIS TASK: the contract screens; a client-facing share link or portal (row C-22, OUT — Rule 1: in v1 the freelancer downloads or prints the contract and sends it themselves through their own email); a recorded client acceptance event (row C-23, OUT — Rule 1; this overrides the AS-31 plan section 12 Q1 default and is recorded in the milestone plan's amendment log); e-signature of any legal weight (row C-24, OUT); our own PDF renderer (row C-25, OUT — the browser's print-to-PDF closes the chain); a second template.
data.title: D1 v1: contract templates and generation (server)

data.note: contracts need the client and contract tables

data.body:
Pulled as the highest-leverage remaining task: it is the last server task, and three tasks sit directly behind it — AS-47 and AS-48 (the contract and read-view screens) and AS-49 (the automated end-to-end verification). AS-45 and AS-46 are also unblocked now, but they gate nothing; this one gates the rest of the line.

Marcus implements. He built the client and contract tables in AS-39 and the invoice lifecycle that references them, and this composes both. Lena has run the last two implementation stages (AS-40 plus its rework) — rotating also keeps either implementer from becoming the only reader of a surface.

Note for the planner: contracts are the one D1 entity with no Stripe involvement at all, so the custody guard and the connected-account rules are not in play. Say that explicitly in the plan's not-in-scope, because every other server task in this app has had a Stripe dimension and an implementer will expect one.

Planned. Templates are code, not files or rows — a frozen declaration with structured body segments, so there is no substitution syntax and therefore no parser to confuse; every text node (template-authored and user-supplied alike) goes through one escaper and no data reaches an attribute position at all. AS-39 §8 Q4 closed: outcome confirmed (no column, no migration), premise overturned — templates ARE versioned and the version rides in template_id, because the M4 text replacement is scheduled rather than hypothetical and an unversioned id would silently redefine every issued row. Immutability is by absence, pinned by the committed route list. One route, POST /contracts, below the boundary. TWO ITEMS FOR THE BOARD/CEO LANE, both in §9: (Q1) nothing in the app creates a client — repos.clients.create has zero non-test callers, and inline client creation is on screens 4 AND 6, so the server half is unowned; default is one shared POST /clients built by whichever of AS-46/AS-47 lands first, never two. (Q2) I am NOT rendering the wireframe's Common Paper CC BY 4.0 attribution line, because this body is not adapted from Common Paper — attributing our own placeholder text to them misstates authorship and makes the document look more authoritative, which works against the legal gate. The mechanism is built and exercised; only the wording differs. Carla can overturn cheaply — it is one string plus a version bump.

Starting implementation in .worktrees/AS-42 on feat/AS-42-contracts, per the plan: templates as frozen code with no parser, one escape function applied to every text node, no data in attribute positions, versioned template ids with the render-reproduces-stored-output invariant, and immutability implemented as route absence. No Stripe surface anywhere in this task.

IMPLEMENTATION COMPLETE (agent:developer-marcus). Branch feat/AS-42-contracts, 2 commits: 6a8c06f (code + tests), 217af54 (apps/invoicing/README.md). Worktree clean, nothing pushed, nothing merged.

== FILES TOUCHED (11) — measured, git diff --stat master...HEAD: 1,627 insertions, 10 deletions ==
NEW (6): lib/contracts/templates.js 210 · lib/contracts/templates/independent-contractor-agreement.js 67 · lib/contracts/render.js 171 · lib/contracts/generation.js 124 · routes/contracts.js 125 · test/contracts.test.js 827
EDITED (5): app.js +10 · test/auth.test.js +10/-4 · test/dependency-policy.test.js +26/-3 · test/harness.test.js +5/-2 · README.md +62/-1

== SUITE: BOTH SERVICES GREEN ==
`test` service (network_mode: none, no key, no egress): 15 files, 369 tests, 351 pass, 0 fail, 18 skipped, exit 0.
The 18 skipped are exactly the stripe-mock cases, none of them mine, all self-skipping on ASC_STRIPE_MOCK_URL: connect.test.js M1/M2/M3, invoices.test.js M1/M2/M3, and stripe-mock.test.js x12 (reachable-and-not-Stripe, strict-version-check, the 7 request-shape rows, Idempotency-Key echo, unknown-parameter rejection, forbidden-shape refusal).
`contract` service (attached to stripe-mock): 369 tests, 369 pass, 0 fail, 0 SKIPPED, exit 0.
All 34 new cases ran and passed in both: T1-T7, B1-B9, N1-N8, P1-P8, Y1-Y2.

== FALSIFICATION: 14 ROWS DEFINED, 15 RUNS EXECUTED, 15 RECORDED ==
Method: `git archive HEAD` extract OUTSIDE the worktree (470 files, sha256 manifest), isolated compose project `ascinvas42mut`. Every row: assert-applied ON DISK with `grep -oF <marker> | wc -l` (never grep -c), then assert-applied INSIDE THE BUILT IMAGE with the same occurrence-accurate grep run in the container, then run, then restore-from-pristine + manifest diff + `git status --porcelain` on the worktree. Rebuilt before every row.
CONTROL BEFORE (unmutated extract): 369/351/0/18, exit 0. CONTROL AFTER (restored extract, rebuilt): 369/351/0/18, exit 0, manifest identical to pristine. So no red below is phantom and no green above is stale.

Row | disk/image | predicted | observed | classification
M1 escaper dropped at slot emission | 1/1 | B1, B3 | B1 B2 B3 B5 B7 N1 P1 P8 | WIDER. The golden string is additionally pinned by B2/B7/N1/P1/P8, and B5's hostile values create attributes once unescaped. Prediction written before the test file existed. Nothing narrowed.
M2 escaper dropped at literal emission | 1/1 | B1, B4 | B1 B4 B7 N1 P1 P8 | WIDER, same golden-pinning cause. B4 (the load-bearing one) fired.
M3 body content changed, version NOT bumped | 1/1 | T3, B1 | T3 B1 B7 N1 P1 P8 | WIDER, same cause. T3 fired — the version-honesty guard this task introduces works in its own direction.
M4 required-value check deleted | 1/1 | N2 only | N2 only | EXACT. Confirms N2 asserts /is required/ specifically, so it cannot be satisfied by the renderer's own downstream throw (that is B9, driven directly).
M5 form-key check widened to all variable names | 1/1 | N8, P3 (P2 green) | N8, P3 | EXACT. P2 stayed green — nonsense keys still rejected.
M6 identity read from req.query | 1/1 | P7 only | P7 only | EXACT.
M7 attribution/licence cross-check disabled | 1/1 | T4 | T4 | EXACT.
M8 `// stripe MUT-M8` in render.js | 1/1 | Y1 only, dependency-policy GREEN | Y1 only; all 4 dependency-policy cases green | EXACT. This is the point: Y1 covers ground no global row covers.
M9 'POST /contracts', removed from ALL_ROUTES only | 2->1/1 | G1, G1b (G2 green) | G1, G1b; G2 green | EXACT. FIRST ATTEMPT FAILED TO APPLY and is reported, not hidden: my pattern '  \'POST /contracts\',\\n' matched BOTH occurrences (the G2 one is the same text at 6-space indent), the edit was refused, and the subsequent run was a vacuous green (369/351/0). The occurrence count read 2 when it had to read 1 and caught it. Re-run anchored on the preceding ALL_ROUTES line.
M10 `// MUT-M10 currency` in render.js | 1/1 | concepts case, message naming money representation + the file | concepts case. MESSAGE: "money representation: found in [lib/contracts/render.js, lib/db/migrations/0001-initial.js, ...], allowed in exactly [lib/db/migrations/0001-initial.js, ...]" | EXACT. The money-word trap is LIVE and scans raw text.
M11 second escapeHtml in routes/contracts.js | 1/1 | concepts case, message naming contract HTML escape | concepts case. MESSAGE: "contract HTML escape: found in [lib/contracts/render.js, routes/contracts.js], allowed in exactly [lib/contracts/render.js]" | EXACT. The row this task adds is live from day one, and M10/M11 are distinguishable by message as the plan requires.
M12a registry emptied (DECLARATIONS = []) | 1/1 | T2, T3, T7 among the red | T1 N1 N2 N3 N4 N5 N6 N7 N8 P1 P2 P3 P5 P7 P8 (15) | NARROWER on the three named cases. See finding F1 — this is the most important divergence in the run.
M12b registry literally `new Map()` (the plan's spelling) | 1/1 | as above | 12 test FILES fail to load, zero named cases | The plan's literal recipe is unrunnable as a named-case probe. See F1.
M13 Date.now() appended to the attribution | 1/1 | B1, B7, N5 | B1 B6 B7 N1 N5 P1 P8 | WIDER (golden pinning + B6's exact attribution paragraph). N5 fired — a non-deterministic renderer breaks reproduction, which is the claim.
M14 mutation route added | 1/1 | P8, G1, G1b, G2, G3, G15 | all six, plus Y2 | WIDER BY ONE, and the extra is mine: Y2 asserts the router registers exactly ['POST /contracts']. Immutability-by-absence is pinned six ways, seven with Y2.

== FINDINGS ==
F1 (recipe defect, and a real one). M12 as written cannot produce its prediction, in EITHER form. (a) The plan's literal `new Map()` leaves DECLARATIONS non-empty, which trips the module-load id-uniqueness check ("two declarations share an id — 1 declared, 0 registered") and kills 12 test FILES at import; node reports file-level failures and zero named cases, so "T2, T3 and T7 must be among the red" is unevaluable. (b) The runnable form (DECLARATIONS = []) leaves T2, T3 and T7 GREEN. That is not a vacuity hole: those three quantify over the exported declaration constant with a committed count asserted FIRST (T2: declared.length 4 and segments.length 13; T3: a digest over the whole declaration; T7: variables.length 4), so emptying the registry cannot make them examine nothing. The registry's own cardinality is asserted by T1, which DID fire. The property M12 exists to protect holds; the probe was aimed at a subject my implementation does not use. Recorded rather than re-aimed, per the "a prediction that misses is a finding" rule.
F2 (observation for the reviewer, not a defect). P4 is green under M12a for the wrong reason: getTemplate runs at step 1, so an empty registry 404s before the client lookup and P4's assertions (404 + "NotFoundError: create" + zero rows) all still hold. P4 cannot by itself distinguish an unknown template from an unknown client. P5 covers the template direction separately and P4's row-count assertion is unaffected, so I left it — flagging it so a reviewer sees it deliberately.
F3 (plan text, non-blocking). §3.5's illustrative output block renders `("Provider")` unescaped, while §3.5 point 2 requires all five of & < > " ' to be escaped. The rule governs; the shipped output is `("Provider")`. B1's golden and B4 pin it. AS-47 should read the rule, not the sample.
F4 (carried forward, already filed). §9 Q1: nothing in the app creates a client. Confirmed against this tree — repos.clients.create still has zero non-test callers. Filed as AS-65; this task adds no client creation and takes an existing clientId, per the tasking message.
F5 (for the CEO). §9 Q2 stands as the plan decided: @1's attribution states the mechanism truthfully and does NOT credit Common Paper for text adapted from nothing. B6 asserts the absence of that credit. Overturning it is a one-string change plus a bumped id and a new digest — cheap, and Carla can call it.

== LITERALS THAT MOVED (13 edits across 3 files — §5.6's 12, plus D1) ==
test/auth.test.js (6, all as §5.6 specified): ALL_ROUTES += 'POST /contracts' · G1 14->15 (count and message) · G1b 13->14 · G2 protected list += 'POST /contracts' · G3 protectedRoutes.length 9->10 · G15 discoverRoutes 14->15. PUBLIC_ROUTES unchanged at 5 — this route is protected.
test/harness.test.js (2 + 1 prose): EXPECTED_TEST_FILES += 'contracts.test.js' (sorted config < connect < contracts) · V2 14->15 (count and message) · "these fourteen files" -> "fifteen" in a comment.
test/dependency-policy.test.js (5): source.length 43->48 (NOT 47 — see D2) · source list += 4 lib/contracts entries + routes/contracts.js · new scanConcept('contract HTML escape', /\bescapeHtml\b/, ['lib/contracts/render.js']) · concepts case name += AS-42 · body-parser allowlist += 'routes/contracts.js' (D1).
NOT-MOVING SET — verified by `git diff --name-only master...HEAD`, every one absent: package.json, package-lock.json (LOCK_ENTRIES still 70), compose.yaml, Dockerfile, .dockerignore, lib/config.js (SCHEMA still 11, prefixed 10), lib/views.js (VIEWS still 1, HEALTH_CHECKS 4), all of lib/db/**, and all 11 other test files (config, health, deploy-shape, assets, connect, db, invoices, repositories, stripe-client, stripe-mock, webhooks). SANCTIONED still 3, manifests still 3. No migration, no config row, no compose/Dockerfile change, no new dependency. CLAUDE.md, root README.md, PHILOSOPHY.md and agents.md untouched.

== DEVIATIONS (7, numbered) ==
D1. §5.7's claim "no allowlist is widened" is FALSE and could not be satisfied. Mounting express.urlencoded per route (§3.4, and required so AS-44's webhook keeps its raw body) necessarily trips the 'body parser' concept row, whose allowlist is exactly three files. Added 'routes/contracts.js' to it — a 13th literal edit §5.6 does not list. Smallest change that satisfies §3.4; what the row actually guards (no app-wide parser in app.js) is unchanged and app.js is still not a member. AC 25 is therefore not met as written: one concept row was ADDED and one was WIDENED.
D2. §8's in-task file split FIRED and was applied as pre-agreed. templates.js measured 259 lines with the declaration inline, past the ~250 line. The declaration moved to lib/contracts/templates/independent-contractor-agreement.js (67 lines, imports nothing); templates.js is now 210 and validates + deep-freezes + registers. Consequence: the source count goes 43 -> 48, not the 47 §5.6 item 9 predicted, and files 9 -> 10.
D3. render.js exports a third symbol beyond §5.2's two: assertCalendarDate(value, field), so generation.js validates a date with exactly the function render.js later formats with. The alternative was two copies of the UTC round-trip calendar check that could drift. formatDate stayed internal.
D4. M3's target file is templates/independent-contractor-agreement.js, not templates.js — the body text moved there under D2.
D5. M7's mutation value is `/* MUT-M7 */ false`, not `true`. My cross-check condition is the negation (!attribution.includes(licence)), so `true` would make it always throw — falsifying the wrong direction. `false` disables the check, which is what the recipe's stated purpose needs.
D6. M12 run in two forms (M12a runnable, M12b the plan's literal) rather than one. See F1.
D7. apps/invoicing/README.md is an 11th file, outside §2's "exhaustive" list. §10 explicitly directs the implementer to apply it ("Not metawork, so the implementer applies it directly"), so the two sections of the plan disagree; I followed §10. It records the frozen-class-name obligation, the route surface, the versioned id, immutability-by-absence, and why @1 does not credit Common Paper.

== SPLIT LINES: ONE CROSSED AND HANDLED, ONE CROSSED AND ESCALATED ==
In-task file split (~250 lines in templates.js): CROSSED at 259. Applied as pre-agreed — see D2. templates.js now 210. No plan amendment needed, per §8.
Task split (source > ~600 lines OR files > 10): CROSSED on lines. Measured 697 total lines across the five source files (210+67+171+124+125) against a ~570 projection — +22%. Excluding the D2 split file, which §8 itself mandated: 630. Code-only (non-comment, non-blank): 319. Files: 10 code/test, 11 counting the §10 README — at or one past the line depending on whether a docs file counts.
MY RECOMMENDATION, and it is a recommendation, not a decision: do NOT split the task. Three reasons, stated with the numbers so the CTO can overrule cheaply. (1) The overage is comment density, not logic — 319 code lines against §8's own ~40%-validation calibration, and the four non-split files sum to 630 against their 570 projection, +10.5%. (2) The work is complete and green in both services with all 14 recipes run; splitting now would mean deleting working, verified code to re-land it. (3) §8 prices the split itself: routes/contracts.js + the 8 P cases + the §5.6 literals would move to a follow-up that BOTH AS-47 and AS-49 must then depend on — two extra graph edges on the last server task on the D1 line, against a saving §8 itself calls "a 30-line saving". I am reporting the measured trigger rather than a feeling, per §8; the ruling is the CTO's or QA's.

== NOTHING LEFT UNDONE within scope ==
No client creation added (AS-65's, per the tasking message). No GET routes (AS-47's). No migration, no schema change, no Stripe surface of any kind, no board ask, no spend, no external service. AS-59 item 3 neither fixed nor depended on — every value this service stores is a validated string, so the repository's JSON.stringify cannot meet a BigInt or a cyclic object through POST /contracts. §10's CLAUDE.md wording is for the metawork layer; I did not apply it.

== DOCKER HYGIENE ==
Own projects only (asc-inv-as42, ascinvas42mut), torn down profile-aware (--profile tools down --remove-orphans, so the profile-gated stripe-mock container went too), all 4 images I built removed, no global prune, stripe/stripe-mock:v0.203.0 left pulled, no stray volumes or networks. asc-invoicing-web-1 (8348) and asc-chat-server-1 (8347) verified still running and untouched throughout.

== WHAT THE REVIEWER SHOULD LOOK AT FIRST ==
1. F1 and the M12 rows — the one probe that did not falsify what it aimed at, and my argument for why the property still holds.
2. D1 — an acceptance criterion (25) that cannot be met as written, and the widening I chose instead.
3. The task-split numbers above — a measured §8 trigger I did not act on, deliberately, and my reasons.
4. lib/contracts/render.js as a whole: it is the security surface, and the claim is that there is no path out of it that emits unescaped text and no path that puts data in an attribute. B5 asserts the second structurally; M1/M2 falsify the first in both directions.

Orchestrator rulings before review.

VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY: 11 files, +1627/-10, nothing outside apps/invoicing/, zero files under lib/db/ (so no migration and SCHEMA_VERSION does not move), and no stripe/connect/webhook file touched — the plan's central not-in-scope claim holds mechanically, not just by assertion.

SPLIT: NOT splitting the task. Source measured 697 lines against a ~570 projection, so section 8's trigger fired and the implementer correctly declined to act on it alone. Three reasons to leave it whole: the overage is comment density (319 lines are code excluding comments), the in-task split at 250 lines already fired and was applied as pre-agreed, and section 8 itself prices the task-level split as two new dependency edges on AS-47 and AS-49 for roughly thirty lines saved. This is the fourth task where a line-count tripwire fired on a plan whose file count was exactly right; the estimate model, not the work, is what keeps missing. Section 8's second trigger (review reaching cycle 2 on scope grounds) remains the backstop.

AC 25 CANNOT BE MET AS WRITTEN — tech-lead item, not a rework trigger. Section 5.7 claims no allowlist is widened, but section 3.4 requires a per-route body parser so the webhook keeps its raw body, and that necessarily trips the body-parser concept row. The two sections are inconsistent and the implementer resolved it the only way that ships, widening the row by exactly one file and recording it. Owen should correct 5.6/5.7; the reviewer should judge against intent.

TWO ITEMS THE REVIEWER SHOULD SEE DELIBERATELY, both self-reported rather than discovered: recipe M12 does not falsify what it aims at in either form (the probe targets a registry the tests do not quantify over), and case P4 passes under one mutant for the wrong reason, with a sibling case covering the real direction. Neither is a defect; both are exactly the kind of thing that stays invisible unless the implementer says it out loud.

AND THE FINDING WORTH KEEPING: M9's first attempt did not apply — the pattern matched two occurrences where it had to match one, and the run that followed was a vacuous green. The occurrence-accurate count caught it. That is the sixth instance of this class today and the first where the corrected discipline caught it before it produced a false result rather than after.

Review stage: assigning agent:qa-priya. Marcus implemented, so implementer != reviewer holds. Priya over Ruben on rotation — he took AS-40 cycle 2 and AS-44 — and because this is the first server task with no Stripe dimension at all, which makes it the one where a reviewer's habit of looking for the custody surface will find nothing and needs to not manufacture something.

REVIEW — AS-42 (agent:qa-priya). VERDICT: PASS. No inline fixes; nothing trivial worth touching. 28/28 acceptance criteria pass (criterion 25 against intent — see C25). Branch feat/AS-42-contracts @ 217af54, unmerged, unpushed. Worktree clean, main checkout carries only this comment's .lattice change. == READ ORDER (disclosed, in the order I actually ran it) == 1. CLAUDE.md Review Gate + Review Rework Loop; PHILOSOPHY.md; my dossier. 2. The plan in full (1,030 lines). 3. The task description ALONE, via `lattice show AS-42 --json` piped through node to print `description` — before any comment. 4. The diff cold: source first, then the four existing-file edits, then test/contracts.test.js read as a document. 5. My own runs, attacks and 18 mutation runs; every verdict below written down BEFORE step 6. 6. The comment stream LAST — implementer report and orchestrator rulings. I read them after forming every number in this comment, and I flag differences in both directions. == WHAT I RAN == Everything in an ISOLATED compose project against a COPY OUTSIDE the worktree: `git`-faithful `cp -R` of apps/invoicing + docs/design/tokens + .dockerignore into scratch, 74 files, sha256 manifest committed before the first mutation. Projects `asc-inv-qa42`, `asc-inv-mut`, `asc-inv-c1` — never `asc-invoicing`. `DOCKER_BUILDKIT=0 COMPOSE_DOCKER_CLI_BUILD=0 docker compose -p -f compose.yaml run --rm --build test`. - Baseline on the branch worktree: 369 tests, 351 pass, 0 fail, 18 skipped, exit 0. - Baseline on the scratch copy: identical (369/351/0/18) — the copy is a faithful instrument. - CARDINALITY BEFORE QUANTIFICATION: 34 unique AS-42 cases (T1-7, B1-9, N1-8, P1-8, Y1-2) RAN; 0 of them skipped. The 18 skips are exactly the pre-existing stripe-mock-gated cases (connect M1-M3, invoices M1-M3, stripe-mock x12), all self-skipping on `ASC_STRIPE_MOCK_URL not set`. AS-42 adds no self-skipping case. - Offline proven, not assumed: from inside the `test` service I attempted `fetch('https://example.com/')` -> refused, EAI_AGAIN. `network_mode: none` is real. - Commit-1-in-isolation: `git archive 6a8c06f` into a fresh tree -> 369/351/0/18, exit 0. Both commits are independently green (commit 2 touches only apps/invoicing/README.md). == THE SECURITY PROPERTY, ATTACKED ON ITS OWN TERMS == The design claims injection is impossible by CONSTRUCTION, not by escaping alone: (1) no parser, (2) one escaper on every text node, (3) no data in an attribute position. I attacked all three with my own instruments, not the suite's. A. 38 payloads x 3 user-controlled fields = 114 documents rendered. Payload set included tag breakouts (`

` inside a value would be emitted as `</script>` — safe — but the surrounding raw-text parsing rules make the whole fragment wrong there), in a URL or `srcdoc` (no percent- or double-escaping), in a JSON string emitted into a script tag (no ` `/` `/`` exactly once inside `.doc-region`, `<%= %>` for everything else, is correct. == THE REPRODUCTION INVARIANT, ESTABLISHED MY OWN WAY == Not by reading N5. I drove 11 contracts through the real HTTP route in one database, then re-rendered EVERY stored row from `getTemplate(row.template_id)` + `JSON.parse(row.variables)` and compared to `row.rendered_html`: 11/11 byte-identical (cardinality first: 11 rows examined). Probing a template changing underneath an issued row: M3 changes `standard terms` -> `standard MUTM3 terms` without bumping `@1`, and T3 (the digest guard THIS task introduces) plus B1, B7, N1, P1, P8 all go red — the version-honesty guard works in its own direction. I also confirmed the snapshot half by hand: renaming the client after issue leaves the stored document unchanged (`variables.clientName` stays the issued value), so `variables` is a snapshot and not a live join. == IMMUTABILITY AS ABSENCE, ATTACKED == - 24 id-bearing mutation requests (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE x {`/contracts/:id`, `/contracts/:id/`, `/edit`, `/void`, `/delete`, `?_method=DELETE`}): ALL 404. The issued document is byte-unchanged afterwards. - `OPTIONS /contracts` advertises `Allow: POST` and nothing else; `OPTIONS /contracts/:id` is a 404 with no Allow header. - `POST /contracts/` (trailing slash) is the SAME create route under Express's non-strict routing — not a second surface, and behind the same guard (cookieless -> 303 /signin). I mis-filed it as a mutation probe on my first pass and correcting that is worth recording. - Walked the built app's router tree independently: 14 routes constructed in my harness config, exactly one matching /contract/i, and it is `POST /contracts`. - The repository exposes exactly `create`, `getById`, `listByFreelancer` — no update path below the route either. - PINNED, not asserted: M14 adds `router.post('/contracts/:id', ...)` and SEVEN cases go red — P8, G1, G1b, G2, G3, G15, plus Y2. Absence is pinned seven ways. == OWNERSHIP, ATTACKED == Two seeded freelancers with real sessions, one client each. - O1: A posts B's clientId -> 404, body `NotFoundError: create\n`, ZERO rows written. - O2: a clientId that never existed -> byte-identical status and body.
